decoys.problem: removeProviderCatalogEntry swallows every lock/write error in a catch that holds only a comment.
decoys.impact: A prune that fails leaves the entry in the cache without telling the caller.
decoys.quote: // Best-effort, like every other write in this module.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: This is the module's consistent, documented posture: every cache writer (saveProviderCatalogCache, clearProviderCatalogCache, updateProviderCatalogEntry) is best-effort because the cache is a courtesy. The JSDoc states the reason and it holds: the next full refresh writes only the providers it looked at, so an undropped entry is not carried over and ages out. The import result does not claim pruning happened, so no caller is misled.

candidate.problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows the snapshot write failure in an empty catch with no comment, then returns { ok: true, path, summary } as if the file was written. The `ok` field is hard-coded true, so it can never report the failure (error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Laws 1-2). This also contradicts the function's own doc comment, which promises it never lets a caller 'ship an empty snapshot believing it holds the operator's providers'.
candidate.impact: syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true), called from loadOrRefreshWith in provider-catalog.ts:270, returns a summary such as '3 provider(s), 2 live' when the pinned file was never written (read-only config dir, full disk, bad destPath). The operator who enabled pinSnapshot for air-gapped use thinks a fallback exists. The next empty refresh then finds no pinned file and silently has nothing to restore. Sites: provider-catalog-snapshot.ts:72-78 is the only write in the new module (checked every try/catch in the diff).
